content.user_title: Audit Java Projects for DDD Compliance
content.value_statement: Large Java projects can accumulate layer violations and inconsistent domain patterns. This skill audits every Java file and produces prioritized, actionable findings.
actual_capabilities: Discovers Java source files while excluding target and test directories.
Groups reviewed files by domain-driven design layer.
Checks package placement, base classes, naming, dependencies, structure, and exception handling.
Detects reverse dependencies, anemic domain models, missing patterns, and exception boundary violations.
Assigns severity levels and reports findings with file locations and suggested fixes.
Produces layer summaries, an ASCII dependency graph, a compliance score, and prioritized recommendations.
limitations: Requires the referenced rule and reference files to be available in the installed skill package.
Targets Java projects that follow the Bookiosk domain-driven design conventions.
Uses source inspection and search results rather than compilation or runtime behavior.
Compliance scores depend on complete file access and correct layer identification.

use_cases.title: Review a release candidate
use_cases.description: Audit the complete Java codebase before release and prioritize architecture violations that could increase maintenance risk.

use_cases.title: Assess a refactoring baseline
use_cases.description: Measure current layer compliance and identify concrete changes before a domain-driven design refactoring effort.

use_cases.title: Learn project conventions
use_cases.description: Generate a structured review that explains required base classes, dependency direction, naming, and exception boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Run a full audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a full DDD compliance audit on this Java project. Report violations by layer and recommend exact fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a first comprehensive project review.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a release review
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the entire project for DDD compliance before release. Prioritize critical dependencies, public identity setters, and exception boundary violations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan architecture refactoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a full DDD audit and organize recommendations into immediate, near-term, and later refactoring priorities. Include affected files and rule references.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when planning a staged architecture improvement.

prompt_templates.title: Compare layers and dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit every Java file against all DDD rules. Compare layer compliance, identify reverse dependencies, explain root causes, and propose a sequenced remediation plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for an advanced cross-layer architecture assessment.

output_examples.input: Run a full DDD audit before the next release.
output_examples.output: The audit reviewed 86 Java files across five layers. It found two critical reverse dependencies, six high-severity rule violations, and eleven convention issues.

output_examples.input: Identify the most urgent domain-layer problems.
output: Critical: The domain layer imports an infrastructure mapper. Move conversion logic into the infrastructure adapter.
High: Order exposes a public identity setter. Change its visibility to protected.
Medium: Customer contains only accessors. Add domain behavior or reconsider its role.

output_examples.output: First remove reverse dependencies. Next correct base classes and exception boundaries. Then address naming, anemic models, documentation, and style findings.

best_practices: Run the audit from the project root so discovery covers every production Java file.
Keep the rule files aligned with the architecture version used by the project.
Review critical dependency findings before lower-severity naming and style issues.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the compliance score as a substitute for reviewing individual findings.
Do not run the audit with missing rule files or inaccessible source directories.
Do not apply suggested base classes without confirming the project uses the expected framework conventions.

faq.question: What projects does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Java projects organized around the Bookiosk domain-driven design layers and base-class conventions.

faq.question: Does the skill modify source files?
faq.answer: No. The workflow discovers and reads Java files, then reports violations and suggested fixes.

faq.question: Are test files included?
faq.answer: No. The documented discovery command excludes test and target directories.

faq.question: What does the audit check?
faq.answer: It checks packages, base classes, naming, dependencies, domain structure, exception handling, missing patterns, and common architecture anti-patterns.

faq.question: How are findings prioritized?
faq.answer: Findings use critical, high, medium, and low severity levels based on architecture impact and convention importance.

faq.question: What files must accompany the skill?
faq.answer: The workflow expects seven rule files and two optional reference files listed in the skill instructions.
